topics.title: US voters weigh ballot measures alongside midterms
topics.summary: Voters across the United States are deciding congressional control as well as 145 proposed laws and constitutional amendments. Measures on issues including voting rules and redistricting show how local ballots can shape national debates.
topics.discussionPrompt: Ballot questions can be surprisingly specific. If your neighborhood got to vote on one everyday improvement, what would you put on the ballot first?

topics.title: UK and EU complete food-trade agreement
topics.summary: The UK and EU completed a deal intended to remove Brexit-era checks on food and animal products. The agreement could make smaller cross-border orders easier, though implementation is expected in 2028.
topics.discussionPrompt: Imagine you run a tiny shop that sells one perfect imported snack. What would be worth the paperwork to keep it on the shelf?

topics.title: Apple flags rising memory-chip costs
topics.summary: Apple said unusually steep memory-chip prices and the cost of serving AI tools could pressure profit margins, despite stronger sales expectations for the holiday season. The warning highlights growing competition for key computer components.
topics.discussionPrompt: If every gadget suddenly became more expensive, which one would you keep repairing for years instead of replacing?

topics.title: UK cyber agency warns about AI-enabled attacks
topics.summary: Britain's National Cyber Security Centre says AI-powered malware is likely to feature in ransomware attacks on critical infrastructure by 2028. The agency says AI may amplify familiar tactics rather than create entirely new threats.
topics.discussionPrompt: A good password manager is not glamorous, but neither is changing every password after a mess. What tiny digital habit makes you feel most organized?

topics.title: Brazil publishes fossil-fuel phaseout roadmap
topics.summary: Brazil released a global roadmap for moving away from fossil fuels, arguing that countries can pair the transition with economic development. The plan aims to shift climate talks toward practical implementation.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a huge goal needs doing, are you more convinced by a bold long-term map or a checklist of small steps you can start today?

topics.title: Gardeners get a climate-planning tool
topics.summary: UK horticultural groups are developing a free tool to help gardeners estimate how plants may cope with future local conditions. It is designed to make climate adaptation more practical for home gardens.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you had a garden that could thrive with almost no fuss, would you fill it with flowers, herbs, vegetables, shade trees, or something gloriously strange?

topics.title: Ruffed grouse decline prompts conservation concern
topics.summary: Falling ruffed grouse numbers have led Ohio to withhold open hunting permits for the first time since 1937. Habitat pressure, West Nile virus and warming conditions are among factors cited in the bird's decline.
topics.discussionPrompt: Some animals become local legends without anyone noticing. Which bird, bug, or small creature do you secretly root for whenever you spot it?

topics.title: Barclays begins some car-finance payouts
topics.summary: Barclays became the first major UK lender to offer payments to some customers who complained about mis-sold car loans. The move comes while the wider compensation scheme remains tied up in legal proceedings.
topics.discussionPrompt: Buying a car involves so much fine print. What is the most confusing purchase you have ever tried to compare: cars, phones, insurance, or something else?

topics.title: Birmingham clubbers rally around nightlife spaces
topics.summary: People in Birmingham's Digbeth district are campaigning to protect clubs and creative spaces as major rail work approaches. The debate spotlights how redevelopment can reshape a city's nighttime culture.
topics.discussionPrompt: Every city needs a place with personality after dark. Would you save the old dance floor, the late-night diner, the tiny cinema, or the weird little shop?

topics.title: Drax site proposed for major AI datacentre
topics.summary: Drax's owner agreed a plan with investors to develop a large AI datacentre at the North Yorkshire power-station site. Supporters cite investment and jobs, while the proposal raises questions about energy and emissions.
topics.discussionPrompt: A giant new data centre needs power, water, land, and neighbors. Which question would you ask first if one were proposed near your town?
